correctness.rationale: The proof builds the full stochastic kernel for every symmetric integer law; an endpoint-centered Rayleigh vector gives the exact universal spectral obstruction. The proposed uniform nonzero-displacement law is evaluated entrywise and has one scalar nonstationary eigenvalue. For shape stability, each fixed-distance graph Laplacian has norm at most 4 and a second-moment spectral inequality forces positive eigenvalue spread; arbitrary unused mass is handled by an exact laziness decomposition. Both boundary n=2 and S=0 are covered. The package checker supplies 15,483 corroborating exact/numerical tests but is not relied on as an all-n proof.

value.rationale: Sampling a uniform target with a symmetric state-independent proposal and hard-wall rejection is a standard physical Monte Carlo design problem. The result solves it globally for all finite lattice widths, proving unique optimal jump weights and an explicit stability penalty for wasted mass and asymmetric step-length choices. It identifies a finite-lattice speedup strictly beyond the 1/2 continuum optimum while preserving exactly 1/2 acceptance. This is a natural, reusable structural design fact, not a selected parameter numerical example.
